questions.question: Who was U.S. president when the country entered World War I?
choices: Theodore Roosevelt
Woodrow Wilson
William Howard Taft
Warren Harding

questions.question: In which year did the United States enter World War I?
What was the American Expeditionary Forces?
choices: An agency selling war bonds
A committee negotiating tariffs
A fleet guarding only U.S. harbors
The U.S. military force sent to Europe

questions.question: Who commanded the American Expeditionary Forces?
choices: Douglas MacArthur
Dwight Eisenhower
John J. Pershing
George S. Patton

questions.question: What did the Selective Service Act of 1917 establish?
choices: A military draft system
A prohibition on war borrowing
A national women's voting amendment
A new international peace organization

questions.question: What name was given to Wilson's 1918 outline for a postwar peace?
choices: The Square Deal
The Fourteen Points
The New Freedom Act
The Atlantic Charter

questions.question: Which country sent the Zimmermann Telegram proposing an alliance with Mexico?
choices: France
Russia
Germany
Italy

questions.question: Why did Germany's unrestricted submarine warfare threaten U.S. interests?
choices: It required Americans to stop producing farm goods
It placed German troops along the U.S.-Canadian border
It transferred control of U.S. ports to Britain
It endangered ships and passengers without ordinary warning procedures

questions.question: How did the Zimmermann Telegram influence U.S. opinion?
choices: It heightened concern about a possible attack involving Mexico
It promised to end Germany's submarine campaign
It guaranteed U.S. membership in a peace organization
It announced the surrender of all German armies

questions.question: Why did the U.S. government sell Liberty Bonds?
choices: To replace all federal taxes permanently
To borrow money from the public for the war effort
To distribute farmland to returning soldiers
To pay reparations to Germany before the war ended

questions.question: How did wartime industrial demand contribute to the Great Migration?
choices: It eliminated racial discrimination in northern cities
It required every southern farm worker to move
It made cotton farming more profitable than factory work
It created northern jobs that attracted many Black southerners

questions.question: What role did the Committee on Public Information play?
choices: It negotiated military surrender terms with Germany
It trained all U.S. combat pilots
It promoted public support for the American war effort
It wrote state constitutions after the war

questions.question: Why did the Espionage and Sedition Acts raise civil liberties concerns?
choices: They were used to punish some antiwar speech and activities
They abolished the military draft
They expanded public access to all military plans
They required direct election of federal judges

questions.question: How did U.S. entry affect the Allied war effort?
choices: It immediately ended fighting on every front
It provided additional troops, supplies, and financial resources
It forced Britain and France to leave the alliance
It made the U.S. responsible for all Allied military decisions

questions.question: Why did the United States not join the League of Nations after World War I?
choices: The League prohibited participation by any republic
Wilson refused to support an international organization
Germany controlled admission and vetoed U.S. membership
The Senate did not approve the Treaty of Versailles

questions.question: Which sequence correctly places U.S. involvement in World War I?
choices: Armistice → U.S. entry → Fourteen Points
Fourteen Points → U.S. entry → Armistice
U.S. entry → Fourteen Points → Armistice
U.S. entry → Armistice → Fourteen Points

questions.question: A 1918 poster urges families to conserve wheat for soldiers. Which aspect of the war does it illustrate?
choices: Civilian participation in mobilizing resources
A campaign to replace voluntary conservation with military enlistment
An effort to reduce exports to every Allied country
A plan to restore the prewar balance of U.S. foreign trade

questions.question: Which statement most accurately connects the Lusitania sinking in 1915 with U.S. entry in 1917?
choices: The United States declared war on the day of the sinking
The sinking shaped opinion, but later developments also contributed to entry
The sinking occurred after American troops reached France
The incident had no effect on diplomatic relations

questions.question: A senator worries that League membership could commit the country to future conflicts. What issue does this argument emphasize?
choices: Whether states should conduct their own foreign policy
Whether the national bank should issue currency
The balance between international cooperation and national independence
The replacement of Congress with an international legislature

questions.question: Which evidence would best support a study of World War I's effects on U.S. workers?
choices: Diplomatic correspondence about European territorial settlements
Military maps showing trench positions on the Western Front
Congressional debates over the League of Nations treaty
Factory employment records and workers' wartime letters
